So Buck does the only reasonable thing. He drives straight to Eddie’s house. “You have to marry me.” Eddie looks at him for approximately three seconds. “Okay.” It’s supposed to be practical. Except Eddie buys Buck an engagement ring because no one actually asked Buck if he wanted to marry him. Then they get married. Then everyone assumes they’ve secretly been together for years. Summary: "I hope I live in your memory the same way you’ll live in mine. You’ll always be there."For Evan Buckley, it was supposed to be nothing more than a stormy night spent driving down iconic Route 66. But fate had other plans, throwing him headfirst into a stranger at a vintage motel in Seligman, Arizona. Beneath the persistent red glow of a neon sign, two lonely souls found an overwhelming, profound connection—no names, no strings, just warmth, surrender, and an unforgettable spark. But when dawn broke, all that remained was the empty highway and an enigmatic note left behind by Eddie.Seven months later, Buck’s high-stakes routine at Station 118 in Los Angeles brings him face-to-face with the man of his dreams in the middle of a rescue. The reunion is inevitable, but Eddie has a life and responsibilities in LA that Buck never could have anticipated. Bathed in the crimson glow of emergency lights—a cruel echo of that desert neon—the two must figure out whether their past was the start of something real, or just a heartbreaking mirage on the open road.
